edits.before: A learner with finite representational resources must decide not only how to change its model, but which changes deserve authority and when additional capacity is worth buying. We develop a finite framework in which the evaluator is part of the state being regulated. A shared quadratic register supplies a common cost ledger and an exact boundary between reuse, arbitration and partition purchase. Relative-entropy regularisation then gives a normalised selector over the actions actually available, with gains evaluated at the states those actions execute. An explicit model/evaluator controller converges under stated damping and coupling conditions, without assuming that convergence establishes adaptive value. We derive weighted free-energy contraction and show that OR aggregation of externally frozen independent update opportunities closes exactly in cumulative hazard. A smaller common-intercept representation has a calculable event-probability error, while its threshold response equals conditional event multiplicity. The same distinction between marginalisation and constrained closure leads to a quantum recovery criterion. A sequence of figures connects the calculations to a matched synthetic policy comparison, including its adverse predictive result. The proposed laws of learning are thus operational requirements on an embodied model-revision scheme: declare its evaluator, price its executed actions, and test what survives a change of representation.
edits.after: A learner with finite representational resources must decide how to change its model, which changes deserve authority and when additional capacity is worth buying. We develop a finite framework in which the evaluator can itself be part of the regulated state. A shared quadratic register supplies a common cost ledger and an exact boundary between reuse, arbitration and partition purchase. Relative-entropy regularisation gives a normalised selector over available actions, with gains evaluated at the states those actions execute. A separately specified model/evaluator controller converges in reuse mode under stated damping and coupling conditions, without assuming that convergence establishes adaptive value. We derive weighted free-energy contraction and show that OR aggregation of externally frozen independent update opportunities closes exactly in cumulative hazard. A smaller common-intercept representation has a calculable event-probability error, while its threshold response equals conditional event multiplicity. The distinction between marginalisation and constrained closure also leads to a quantum recovery criterion. A matched synthetic policy comparison exposes the difference between consistent action pricing and predictive success, retaining the adverse predictive result. The proposed laws of learning are operational requirements on an embodied model-revision scheme: declare its evaluator, price its executed actions, and test what survives a change of representation.

edits.before: Making that purchase endogenous introduces a further state: the mechanism that estimates gain and authorises cost. Our explicit reuse-mode controller shows that such a mechanism can converge together with the model under stated conditions. It also shows why an equation of mutual determination is not a convergence theorem. The damping, coupling, parent drive and update order carry the result. A switched architecture with a learning parent must include those additional states in its own analysis.
edits.after: An endogenous evaluator introduces a further state. Our explicit reuse-mode controller shows that its authority coordinate can converge together with the model under stated conditions. It does not implement or establish convergence of a capacity-purchase mechanism. The purchase boundary remains a static comparison, and the tracking policies use their own fixed scoring rule. The damping, coupling, parent drive and update order carry the reuse-mode result. A switched architecture with a learning parent must include those additional states in its own analysis.
edits.reason: Remove the implication that a convergent capacity-purchase mechanism was demonstrated.

Useful adaptation to noisy observations can occur between the designated latent shifts.
